study type: Cross-sectional study (derived from an observational cohort)
exposure: Maternal education level (secondary vs primary school)
Mode of birth (caesarean section vs vaginal birth)
Proximity to clinic (long vs short distance)
outcome: Optimal well-care visit retention up to 18 months
cohort: The study included 481 adolescent mothers (10-19 years) and their 502 children (aged >=19 months) from the Eastern Cape, South Africa.
finding: Only about one-third (36.1%) of children of adolescent mothers achieved optimal well-care visit retention up to 18 months, with retention being highest among children in rural areas, whose mothers had secondary education, born via caesarean section, and living closer to the clinic.
mod_finding: Children born via caesarean section had higher optimal well-care visit retention compared to those born via vaginal birth (aOR=1.65).
cross-section timing: Data were collected when children were at least 19 months old, assessing well-care visit retention up to 18 months.
